create_entry.default: The sensor stays unknown until you teach it both states. Go to **Settings** > **Devices & services** > **Helpers**, select the sensor, select the settings icon, then **Local vision options**. Teach one frame of each state, for example door open and door closed. If a state is not visible right now, teach it later.

error.blank_frame: The camera shows nothing, for example because it is offline or covered. Check the camera and try again.
error.blank_region: There is nothing to compare in this region, for example because it shows a plain surface. Make the region larger or move it to a part with some detail.
error.invalid_frame: The camera returned an image that Home Assistant can't read. Check the camera's settings and try again.
error.invalid_horizontal_range: The left edge must be smaller than the right edge.
error.invalid_vertical_range: The top edge must be smaller than the bottom edge.

data_description.bottom: Where the region ends, in percent of the frame height from the top edge.
data_description.left: Where the region starts, in percent of the frame width from the left edge.
data_description.right: Where the region ends, in percent of the frame width from the left edge.
data_description.top: Where the region starts, in percent of the frame height from the top edge.

region.description:
![Current frame with the region outlined]({preview})

Choose the part of the frame the sensor watches. 0 is the left or top edge of the frame, 100 the right or bottom edge. The next step shows the result.

Put the region around what changes, such as the door itself. Leave out things that move for other reasons, such as people, plants, or things that get moved around.

You can't change the region later without adding the sensor again.
region.title: Choose the region

region_confirm.description:
![Current frame with the region outlined]({preview})

The sensor only looks at the outlined region.

menu_option_descriptions.finish: Create the sensor with this region.
menu_option_descriptions.region: Go back and adjust the edges.

region_confirm.title: Check the region

data_description.device_class: What the region shows. This sets the state names, such as Open and Closed or Detected and Clear, and the icon.
data_description.entity_id: The camera that shows what you want to watch.
data_description.name: For example, Garage door. The sensor is added to the camera's device, so the device name is shown in front, for example Garage camera Garage door. Don't repeat the camera name here.

user.description: Create a binary sensor that recognizes the state of a part of the camera view, such as a garage door that is open or closed. You teach it with example frames from the camera. Everything runs locally.

camera_unavailable.message: Could not get a frame from {entity_id}: {error}

invalid_frame.message: The camera returned an image that could not be decoded: {error}

abort.not_loaded: The sensor is not loaded right now. Check it under **Settings** > **Devices & services** > **Helpers**, then open the options again.
abort.teach_successful: The frame was taught. To teach another one, open the options again. Teach more frames when the region looks different, for example at night or in the other state.

error.blank_frame: The camera shows nothing, for example because it is dark or offline. A new frame is shown above. Try again.
error.blank_region: The region in this frame has nothing to compare, for example because it is dark or shows a plain surface. A new frame is shown above. Try again when the region shows more detail.
error.nothing_selected: Select at least one frame to remove.

menu_option_descriptions.remove: Remove frames taught with the wrong state or that no longer match the view.
menu_option_descriptions.teach: Take the current camera frame and tell the sensor what it shows.

data_description.frames: Each entry shows the state the frame was taught as and when it was taught.

remove.description: Remove frames that were taught with the wrong state or that no longer match the view, for example after the camera was moved. If a state has no frames left, the sensor is unknown until you teach that state again.
remove.title: Remove taught frames

data_description.state: Only teach a frame that clearly shows one state.

teach.description:
![Current frame with the region outlined]({preview})

Teach at least one frame of each state. More frames in different light, such as day, night, or with the lights on, make the sensor more reliable.

Frames taught so far: {counts}. The sensor shows unknown while it is unsure.
teach.title: Teach the current frame
